recipes.name: Spicy Cream of Asparagus Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 pound fresh asparagus spears, trimmed and halved crosswise
1 large Idaho potato, peeled and diced
salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 dash hot pepper sauce (such as Tabasco®), or to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Cook and stir onion in butter until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Pour chicken broth over onions and bring to a boil.
Stir in asparagus and potato; cover and cook until asparagus spears are tender, about 8 minutes.

Pour the soup into a blender, filling the pitcher no more than halfway full. Hold down the lid of the blender with a folded kitchen towel, and carefully start the blender, using a few quick pulses to get the soup moving before leaving it on to puree. Puree in batches until smooth and pour into a clean pot.
Season with salt, black pepper and hot sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Cream of Asparagus Soup
raw_recipe.description: Jalapeno peppers and a dash of hot sauce add heat to this simple cream of asparagus soup.

review.reviewBody: This is a fantastic recipe..I love the slight hint of jalapeno. I made one minor change to the recipe, added some cilantro and it added a little bit more flavor and color to the soup! Thanks for the recipe.

Great soup! Even my picky eaters loved it. I added a couple extra steps because I just can't bring myself to follow any recipe to the letter. First of all, strain the asparagus after blended. I use a French sieve, or chinois, to extract all the pulp. Then, I boiled the diced potatoes separately and added them after blending. Also added a cup of diced cooked chicken breast and made a meal of it. I doubled the portions so I would have a few servings left for lunch this week.

LOVED IT! Tweaked it just a bit though, adding 1 large jalapeño, sautéed with onion; added a little more potato so I could cut down on the cream, which I also cut by using half NF milk and half cream; skipped tobasco; added veggie seasoning to enhance flavor. Also, used a stick blender and creamed it all up right in the pot. Served with Asiago ciabatta croutons - YUM!

I loved this soup more than my usual cream of asparagus soup. The jalapeno added extra flavor to it. I sauteed the Jalapeno with the onion in butter before adding the broth and the other veggies. I cooked for 20 minutes then blended with immersion stick blender and used half and half for cream. The soup did have some strings in it, which could happened with any asparagus soup, not just this one. If this happened to you just stain the whole thing before serving.

Doubled it, added jalapeno into the saute to bring out the heat, also added garlic. fresh asparagus out of my garden and used a stick blender as well, left tips out and added at the end, and have also added mushrooms all good. Very versatile and quick recipe for a great soup.

This may be the best soup I have ever made! I added 2 handfuls of chopped fresh spinach and 1/2 tsp. garlic powder. I only blended 1/2 of the soup, to have some pieces of goodness to chew! I also used almond milk instead of the cream to cut some fat and calories. Springtime means asparagus, and this is a delicious way to use it!!!!!!!!

Good but it could use a little tweaking to enhance the flavor. I added garlic and put out Parmesan and lemon wedges to use if people wanted and that helped, but it still needed something. Next time I’ll try adding another half pound or so of asparagus and see if that’s what it needs. Mine was not at all stringy, and I just used an immersion blender to mix it.

Quick and very easy. I ended up buying pencil thin asparagus in BJ's and blended the soup while it was in the pot with an immersion blender. It was not stringy. I used two jalapeño peppers and it was NOT spicy at all. Since I do like spicy I did add hot pepper sauce to mine! I would make it again.

Really enjoyed this recipe and so easy to prepare.

Made the following changes:
EVOO instead of butter.
Added 2 cloves Garlic.
Habanero instead of Jalapeno.. Ole'!
Lowfat milk and cornstarch instead of heavy cream.
Added asparagus tip in the end instead of pureeing them.

Delicious!
This soup turned out really good. Since I didn't have heavy cream, I used half and half, then added sour cream to individual servings. This really added to the flavor and zest!!

Super tasty and super easy. I made this with one batch of asparagus, which measured out at 8 oz, so I halved the recipe. I think the whole soup was done in about 20 minutes! I chopped off the pretty ends of the asparagus and microwaved them for about 1-2 minutes (mine were very skinny), and placed them on top of the soup. This is a great way to use that really skinny asparagus. A KEEPER!
Sorry for the not so pretty bowl. Added quite a bit of spices and it was awesome.
No changes, its perfect. I ve made it several times and family just loves it. Its the BEST, Thanks for the reeipe, I love it. Ginger

Good soup that’s quick and easy to make! I didn’t have a jalapeño, so I left it out. Hubby liked it without the heat, I added hot sauce to my bowl. We both enjoyed it and I plan to make it again. Thanks for the recipe!😋
I followed the recipe. It was delicious and easy to make. It was not overly spicy.
Used red pepper flakes instead of jalapeño

I made the recipe but omitted the spicy hot ingredients. Simply because my husband can’t handle it even though I would’ve liked it myself. I did add a little garlic as one reviewer suggested and I thought the soup is fantastic. Will make this again and again. Even my picky 11-year-old adored it! No soup leftovers.
Creamy and flavorful without the dairy. Love the heat.
Excellent soup.
Followed the instructions and it turned out perfect !
